nodes.name: CoP nanoarray synthesis
nodes.procedure: Binder-free CoP nanoarrays synthesized on Ni foam via topotactic phosphidation strategy from Co precursor (reference [20]).
nodes.source_text: Our pioneering work in 2014 proposed a topotactic phosphidation strategy to synthesize binder-free CoP nanoarrays...

nodes.name: Electrochemical CoPi formation
nodes.procedure: CoPi@CoP was prepared by electrochemical treatment of CoP in a sodium phosphate solution.
nodes.source_text: CoPi@CoP was prepared by electrochemical treatment of CoP in a sodium phosphate solution.

nodes.description: AEMWE stability test at 0.5 A/cm² with alkaline seawater
nodes.source_text: the voltage-time response shows that the activity of the CoPi@CoP/NF||NiFe LDH/NF pair can be maintained at 0.5 A cm⁻² and an elevated reaction temperature for at least 400 h without a detectable loss (Figure 3f,g)

nodes.description: AEMWE performance with alkaline seawater electrolyte
nodes.source_text: Directly utilizing a piece of CoPi@CoP/NF or a piece of CoP/NF as the cathode in the flow-type AEMWE can both lead to good performance, and the CoPi@CoP/NF||NiFe LDH/NF pair shows higher j than that of CoP/NF||NiFe LDH/NF

nodes.description: HER performance comparison with Pt/C at same mass loading
nodes.source_text: the activity of powder CoPi@CoP/NF is better than that of a commercial Pt/carbon (Pt/C)/NF electrode with the same catalyst loading under high current operation conditions (Figure 3e)

nodes.description: Large area electrode HER performance 4 cm² and 9 cm²
nodes.source_text: electrodes with large geometric areas of 4 and 9 cm² were fabricated... scaling the electrode area from 0.25 to 9 cm² does not reduce the alkaline HER activity

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of CoPi@CoP/NF differs slightly from CoP/NF and shows declined peak intensities, confirming crystalline nature of CoP and amorphous state of CoPi.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of CoPi@CoP/NF differs slightly from that of CoP/NF and shows declined peak intensities (Figure 2b), confirming the crystalline nature of CoP and the amorphous state of CoPi.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co L-edge XAS data of CoPi@CoP are not similar to CoP, indicative of higher oxidation states and greatly changed chemical environments for Co species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Their main features of Co L-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) data are not similar (Figure 2c), which is indicative of higher oxidation states and greatly changed chemical environments for Co species of CoPi@CoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show self-supporting nanoarray features for both CoP/NF and CoPi@CoP/NF; anodic treatment leads to rougher surface especially at nanowire tips without losing 3D nanoarray architecture.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of CoP/NF (Figure 2d) and CoPi@CoP/NF (Figure 2e) illustrate self-supporting features of the CoP nanoarray and CoPi@CoP nanoarray... A quick anodic treatment of CoP/NF leads to a rougher surface (Figure 2d-g), especially for the nanowire tip part (Figure 2f,g), but without losing the 3D nanoarray architecture (Figure 2e).

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructured material with fibrous or tubular morphology, rough surface texture, and nanoscale features
Higher magnification inset showing nanofiber details

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping for CoP/NF shows Co:P atomic ratio ≈0.9:1; for CoPi@CoP/NF shows average atomic ratio ≈1 (Co):0.8 (P):1.5 (O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping for CoP/NF (Figure S2, Supporting Information) collects enough Co as well as P signals, and the Co-to-P atomic ratio in the selected areas is ≈0.9:1... After an electrochemical treatment, the distribution of Co, P, and O for CoPi@CoP/NF obtained from different synthesis batches (Figure S3, Supporting Information) shows that phosphates are formed on CoP, with the average atomic ratio of ≈1 (Co):0.8 (P):1.5 (O).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show significantly rougher surface of CoPi@CoP compared to CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images give more details, and the surface of CoPi@CoP is significantly rougher than that of CoP (Figure S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms CoP formation with lattice spacing of 2.8665 Å for (011) facet; CoPi@CoP shows layer of low-crystallinity materials and amorphous regions confirmed by diffuse haloes in FFT patterns.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of CoP is confirmed by lattice fringes in Figure 2l, and the measured lattice spacing of 2.8665Å is larger than the standard spacing corresponding to the (011) facet, i.e., 2.8290 Å... Diffuse haloes, instead of clear spots, in the fast Fourier transform (FFT) image for the selected area (Figure 2o,p) are typical of amorphous materials.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM elemental mapping indicates Co, P, and O are distributed homogeneously in CoPi@CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Element mapping indicates that Co, P, and O are distributed homogeneously in CoPi@CoP (Figure 2r).

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface and internal (etching depth 20 and 50 nm) XPS signals show Co valences gradient with depth in CoP, reduced surface P proportions after CoPi introduction, nanometer-thick CoPi coverage over CoP with varying chemical states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surface and internal (etching depth levels: 20 and 50 nm) X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) signals were collected to further reflect (near)surface chemistry states... XPS data (Figures S7, S8, Supporting Information) and other characterization results imply the following findings: 1) Co valences of CoP show a gradient with depth... 3) CoPi with a nanometer thickness generally covers the most part of underlying CoP, but it is not completely dense.

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi-in situ and in situ Raman spectroscopy reveals evolution of phosphate/hydrophosphate species on CoPi@CoP with bands at 979.7-988.1 cm⁻¹ (ν₁-PO₃ of HPO₄²⁻) and 1064.1-1068.4 cm⁻¹ (PO₄³⁻/H₂PO₄⁻), more abundant than on CoP; also shows altered interfacial water structures with reduced 4-HB·H₂O proportion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy probes the catalyst structural evolution and interface local environments (Figure 5a,b)... the Raman spectra of CoPi@CoP/NF present notable bands located in the range of 979.7-988.1 cm⁻¹, which are assigned to protonated phosphorus species and should be attributable to the bending mode of PO₃ (ν₁-PO₃) of HPO₄²⁻... At -1.5 V_Hg/HgO, 2-HB·H₂O is almost the exclusively detectable component on CoPi@CoP/NF.
